name: Mike Klein
bio: Mike Klein is an independent candidate for Florida's 3rd Congressional District in 2026. A fifth-generation Floridian raised in Gainesville, he graduated from West Point, served as an Army infantry officer in Operation Desert Storm, and later worked in international business and economic development. He co-founded and chairs Warrior Centric Health, a nonprofit focused on veterans' health care.

platform.point: Ban partisan gerrymandering, corporate PACs and dark money, and bar members of Congress from trading stocks.
Calls for 'ICE Out', shifting resources to professional law enforcement and guaranteeing due process for everyone on US soil.
Treat war as a last resort, rely on diplomacy and multilateral leadership, and insist Congress exercise its war powers.
Raise the cap on Social Security payroll contributions so higher earners pay more into the system.
Supports a basic income floor for all families to help workers adjust to an AI-driven economy.
Create a modern Civilian Conservation Corps and expand youth apprenticeship programs.
Break up prescription drug monopolies to make health care more affordable and accessible.
Fully fund veterans' health care, mental health services and military transition support.

economy.evidence: His platform proposes raising the Social Security contribution cap on the wealthy, enforcing antitrust rules and building local supply chains.

welfare.evidence: He backs a basic income for all families and says every American should have access to affordable health care.

immigration.evidence: His platform calls for 'ICE Out' and says every person on American soil is entitled to due process.

foreign.evidence: He favors diplomacy, multilateral leadership and soft power while calling war a last resort, and says he opposed the Iraq War.

tech.evidence: General statement: his platform calls for enforcing antitrust rules so small businesses can compete, without naming tech-specific measures.

notes: Read the campaign site (home, 5 Pillars, Meet Mike) and Florida Politics launch coverage via its Wikipedia-cited archive; no questionnaire answers found. Positions on abortion, guns, policing, energy, education and religion remain unknown.

name: Mike Sell
bio: Mike Sell is the Florida Forward Party candidate for Florida's 4th Congressional District in 2026. Raised in a Navy family, he began working in minimum-wage jobs as a teenager and later held executive roles in operations, with work in the healthcare and human resources industries. He has founded several volunteer organizations.

platform.point: Fund public education.
Enact what he calls sensible gun legislation.
End price gouging on rent, groceries, health care, prescriptions and education, and fight for higher wages.
Raise taxes on the rich.
Champion a universal basic income.
Defend bodily autonomy.
Divest from overseas conflicts.
Get money out of politics, set term limits and draw fair district maps.

economy.evidence: His platform lists taxing the rich, ending price gouging on rent, groceries and health care, and higher wages.

welfare.evidence: His platform says he will champion a universal basic income.

liberty.evidence: General statements: he lists defending bodily autonomy (abortion) and enacting sensible gun legislation (guns).

foreign.evidence: General statement: his platform calls for divesting from overseas conflicts.

tech.evidence: General statement: his platform calls for reining in exploitative technologies.

education.evidence: General statement: his platform lists funding public education.

notes: Read the campaign home page; the 'A Plan for Us' page loads by script and returned no readable text, and no questionnaires or news coverage were found. Immigration, policing, energy and religion positions remain unknown.

name: Todd Schaefer
current_role: Realtor; retired Navy nuclear reactor operator
bio: Todd Schaefer is an independent candidate for Florida's 4th Congressional District in 2026 and also ran for the seat in 2024. Raised in Anderson, Indiana, he joined the Navy in 1998, qualified as a nuclear reactor operator, served on several submarines and retired in 2018 from Kings Bay. He lives in Fernandina Beach and works as a realtor.

platform.point: His first bill would be an American Prosperity Card Act: free Treasury-backed debit accounts paying the Treasury rate, with capped swipe fees.
Supports a single-payer health system and says profit should be removed from health care.
Close the depreciation tax break for single-family rentals and limit 30-year mortgages for investor-owned rental homes.
Tie the federal minimum wage to inflation.
Cut defense spending, redirect funds to domestic priorities and end what he calls endless wars.
Rethink US foreign policy toward diplomacy and away from sanctions, tariffs and use of force.
Opposes Citizens United and SpeechNow rulings and wants to close revolving doors between government and special interests.
Supports ranked choice voting efforts.

economy.evidence: He backs an inflation-indexed minimum wage, capped card swipe fees, closing investor housing tax breaks and stronger labor unions.

welfare.evidence: His issues page supports a single-payer health care system.

liberty.evidence: On speech, he pledges to defend First Amendment rights against government overreach and broader 'hate speech' definitions; other liberty issues are not addressed.

security.evidence: His proposed card program bars surveillance of account holders and gives a private right of action for privacy violations.

foreign.evidence: He calls for reducing defense spending, ending endless wars and shifting toward diplomacy over sanctions and force.

notes: Read the campaign site (issues, subpages, Meet Todd, Why Run Independent, news); the only forum listed was an Indivisible Jax event with no transcript found. Immigration, energy, tech, education and religion positions remain unknown.

name: Andrew Parrott
current_role: Region 6 Alternate Representative, Libertarian Party of Florida
bio: Andrew Parrott is the Libertarian Party nominee for Florida's 6th Congressional District in 2026. His campaign is based in Ocala, and the Libertarian Party of Florida lists him as an alternate representative for its Region 6.
notes: Found his campaign site through the Libertarian Party of Florida candidate page, but it holds only a quotation about limiting government and contact details, with no issue positions. No questionnaires, debates or news coverage were found, so all 10 topics remain unknown.

name: Christopher Dennison
bio: Christopher "Chris" Dennison is the Libertarian Party nominee for Florida's 7th Congressional District in 2026. Raised in Jacksonville, he served in the Air Force on active duty from 2002 to 2004 and then in the Reserves, worked in banking, and coached youth football in Volusia and Seminole counties from 2009 to 2021. He describes himself as a classical liberal who joined the Libertarians around 2020.

platform.point: End overseas deployments, close unneeded bases and bring troops home.
End foreign aid and require countries hosting US troops to pay for them.
Remove Flock and Axon camera and license-plate systems from public spaces to protect Fourth Amendment rights.
End qualified immunity for all government employees.
Says abortion is a state matter and he will not vote to give the federal government power over it either way.
Opposes the death penalty, citing the risk of executing innocent people.
Let veterans take their health benefits to any doctor they choose instead of only VA facilities.
Says the federal government should stay out of decisions about building data centers on private land.

economy.evidence: General statement: he describes himself as a classical liberal who backs free markets, private property and limited government.

security.evidence: He would end qualified immunity and remove Flock and Axon surveillance systems from public spaces.

foreign.evidence: He calls for ending foreign aid, ending deployments, closing unneeded bases and charging host nations for US troops.

notes: Found and read the campaign site (home and platform pages); FEC confirms the committee is based in Deltona, and no questionnaires or news coverage were found. His abortion stance is states-first and was not scored; immigration, energy, tech, education, welfare and religion remain unknown.

name: Andrew Underwood
bio: Andrew Underwood is the Libertarian nominee for Georgia's 14th Congressional District in 2026. He ran for the Georgia House of Representatives' 2nd District in 2022 and was the Libertarian Party of Georgia's candidate in the 2026 special election for the same congressional seat. His campaign is based in Northwest Georgia.

platform.point: Will not vote to extend Obamacare subsidies and opposes further government intervention in health care.
Signed the U.S. Term Limits pledge for three House terms and two Senate terms.
Would vote for a nationwide data center moratorium while Congress considers privacy protection laws.
Opposes companies such as Flock Safety storing data and building profiles of people in public.
Calls for immigration reform that addresses root causes of unauthorized crossings.
Opposes tariffs, saying Americans bear their cost, and favors free market enterprise.
Supports legislation for more ICE transparency and congressional oversight of DHS shootings.

economy.evidence: He opposes tariffs and says free market enterprise is the only solution for the economy.

welfare.evidence: He says he will not extend Obamacare or support other government intervention in health care.

liberty.evidence: General statement: his launch release cites individual liberty through free expression (speech); other liberty issues are not addressed.

security.evidence: He opposes corporate surveillance profiling such as Flock Safety's and backs more oversight and transparency for ICE and DHS.

immigration.evidence: General statement: he praises historic open immigration and calls for root-cause immigration reform to fix border security.

tech.evidence: He says he would vote for a nationwide moratorium on data centers while Congress considers privacy protection laws.

notes: Read the campaign site (home, issues, press releases) and Wikipedia's special-election page, which lists a February 2026 GPB forum video he joined but whose content was not reviewed. Foreign policy, energy, education and religion positions remain unknown.

name: Jordan Conley
bio: Jordan Conley is the Green Party nominee for Hawaii's 1st Congressional District in 2026 and lives in ʻAiea. He describes himself as a coach, fitness professional, teacher and community organizer, and in 2016 he co-founded Hapa Mana, a nonprofit focused on at-risk youth.

platform.point: Would push for a vote on national universal health care, or a state-level universal health care bill if that fails.
Supports an empty-homes tax, taxing Airbnb rentals, Housing First policies and apartments under the Hawaiian Homestead Act.
Supports full repeal of the Jones Act.
Wants the US military removed from Hawaii and from other countries, calling himself anti-imperialist.
Opposes using liquefied natural gas as a bridge fuel and favors solar, hydro, geothermal and wind.
Calls for fast, humane immigration hearings that judge each case individually.
Supports a higher minimum wage and a universal basic income.
Supports ranked choice voting, public campaign financing and a ballot-access amendment.

economy.evidence: He backs an empty-homes tax, taxing Airbnb and a higher minimum wage, while also supporting repeal of the Jones Act.

welfare.evidence: He told Civil Beat his first priority would be a vote on national universal health care, and his site lists universal basic income.

security.evidence: He criticized the 1994 federal crime bill for militarizing police and harming Black, brown and poor families.

immigration.evidence: He calls for quick trials and humane, case-by-case judgments for immigrants rather than a stated enforcement expansion.

foreign.evidence: He says he would work to remove the US military from Hawaii and opposes US forces in any other country.

energy.evidence: He opposes LNG as a bridge fuel toward Hawaii's 100% renewable goal and favors expanding solar and other renewables.

notes: Used his Civil Beat general-election questionnaire and his campaign site (home, about); the Green Party of Hawaii candidate page returned errors. Positions on abortion, guns, tech regulation, school choice and religion remain unknown.

name: Nathan Berning
bio: Nathan Berning is running as an independent (nonpartisan) candidate for Hawaii's 1st Congressional District in 2026. He co-founded and helped lead a national nonprofit that supports pregnant women in crisis, and stepped away from its governance to run for office.

platform.point: Opposes abortion and proposes a 'Right to Keep' commitment of practical support so no mother chooses abortion because of poverty.
Wants support around pregnancy, birth, housing, health care, childcare and work for mothers who want to keep their children.
Seeks federal housing and infrastructure partnerships and tax policy aimed at working families.
Reduce needless federal barriers and improve access to capital for local businesses, trades, agriculture and responsible tourism.
Prioritize clean water, healthy land, local food capacity and responsible energy policy with transparent federal decisions.
Pledges to work with either party and run a transparent, accessible office focused on constituent service.

welfare.evidence: General statement: he calls for practical support with housing, health care and childcare for pregnant women and families, without naming a program.

liberty.evidence: On abortion, his campaign site says plainly that he opposes it; other liberty issues are not addressed.

notes: Found and read his campaign site; he did not appear in Civil Beat's candidate questionnaires, and no news or forum coverage was found. His economic statements are mixed and general, and positions on most other topics remain unknown.
